# Polyarthritis and oligoarthritis

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Rheumatology and immunology > Joint diseases > Polyarthritis and oligoarthritis*

[Original Article Link](/library/dv0o_3)

---

## Summary

<u>Polyarthritis</u> and <u>oligoarthritis</u> are conditions characterized by swelling and/or <u>pain</u> affecting multiple <u>joints</u>. Causes are diverse and include infections, autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, crystal deposition, and <u>osteoarthritis</u>. The most common causes of <u>polyarthritis</u> are hand <u>osteoarthritis</u> and <u>rheumatoid arthritis</u>. Clinical evaluation involves a focused history and <u>physical examination</u> to assess <u>joint</u> involvement patterns and <u>pain</u> characteristics and evaluate for <u>synovitis</u> and extra-articular symptoms. <u>Synovitis</u> and/or extra-articular features often suggest an inflammatory or autoimmune cause. Diagnosis varies based on the suspected condition but may include <u>laboratory studies</u> (e.g., <u>CBC</u>, <u>inflammatory markers</u>) and imaging (e.g., <u>x-rays</u>) of affected <u>joints</u>. Additional studies and specialist referral may be considered based on clinical suspicion. Management varies depending on the underlying cause and may include symptomatic treatment, disease-modifying agents, and/or treatment of infection.
